naslov: Lessons and Messages of the Hijrah

segmenti.tekst: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون.

Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind, and blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected congregation, our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, strove to the utmost to convey this call to people.
At the beginning of the revelation, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, called in secret. And that was not a problem for the polytheists; in that period… there were not many problems.
When does the problem arise? When the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, begins to call people to Islam publicly. Then persecution and torture appear.

After that, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, permits the believers to make the hijrah (emigration), first to Abyssinia, and after that to Medina, where Islam goes, where Islam makes its hijrah.

The hijrah, dear brothers, we can freely say, is the greatest event in the history of mankind. An event that changed the course of human history. An event full of lessons and messages, and we will mention a few.
The first lesson or message of the hijrah is that the gaze, or the arrows, of the disbelievers and enemies are always aimed at whom?
At the learned. At learned people. You know that the polytheists wanted to kill the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, thinking that they would thereby extinguish the light of Islam.

After that, the killing of Umar, Uthman, Ali – all of them the best and most learned people. We have the same throughout the history of Islam. You yourselves know that after the Second World War, at Hadžet, the most learned and best among us were killed.

Why? In order to extinguish the light of this religion. And a few years ago as well, you yourselves know at whom those arrows were aimed – at the late mufti. We all know that. When we extinguish a light, then what? Darkness falls.

Darkness falls. That is why the believers should love their learned, respect their learned, their elite – but those who are recognized among the people, those whom the believers truly love. And woe, dear brothers, to those whom the believers do not love.

Woe to those whom the believers do not love and do not accept as their leaders. The second lesson of the hijrah is that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, raised the sanctity of this religion above homeland, above wealth, above everything.

Homeland, dear brothers, and wealth have no value without religion. An example of this, an example of this is the hijrah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. We know that Mecca is the most sacred place, yet the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, left it – why?
Because he could not worship Allah as it should be done. Also among the lessons is purity, or cleanliness, of the heart and the heart's distance from personal desires.

We know that before he made the hijrah, they offered the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, gold, to make him king, they offered him women; there is nothing they did not offer him, they offered him everything. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, refused all of it.
Why? For the sake of Allah and for the sake of this call, for the sake of this religion. Today, unfortunately, we have a person selling himself for a job. For a few coins, dirhams, dinars, euros.

A person should rise above these things and know what the highest goal is. Because this life is short. This life, dear brothers, is short; it should be lived with dignity, and the way, and the way it should be. Also, one of the lessons of the hijrah is the obligation of relying on Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

That a person relies on Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and takes the prescribed means. Let us look: the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, when he made the hijrah, did not just go out and head for Medina; rather, together with Abu Bakr, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), he planned the journey well.
Where will they go? How will they go? He hired the best guide. And so a person too: he should do everything that is up to him, and after that rely on Allah.

Also, dear brothers, sabr (patience). The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was patient for ten years in Mecca. Patience is necessary. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient.” And enjoin one another to truth, and…

to patience. It cannot be done without patience. The believer must be patient in order to reach the goal. And when the believer is patient and gives up something for the sake of Allah, Allah will give him something better than it. And that is one of the lessons
of the hijrah. The believers left their property, their houses, they left everything for the sake of Allah, and Allah granted them that after a few years they conquered both Persia and Byzantium.

Also, among the lessons and messages of the hijrah is that the believer should be moderate both in blessing and in hardship. We know that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, left Mecca with dignity.
Without anyone humiliating him, without anyone buying him, bribing him. When he entered Mecca, he entered with dignity. He entered with dignity, without taking revenge on anyone.
The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not take revenge. He did not repay evil with evil. And that should be a lesson, a lesson for every believer: not to repay evil with evil, but with good.

That is our religion, dear brothers. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Whoever enters his house is safe.” And the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, forgave everyone. And he could have killed everyone, slaughtered them.

But he did not want to, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not want to. And that is a message to all of us, that we adorn ourselves with those virtues that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, had. And the last lesson or message, dear brothers, is that on this path, the path of truth, the path of Islam, sacrifice is needed.

Sacrifice is necessary, dear brothers. It cannot be done without sacrifice. Whoever thought that he would worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as it should be done and enjoy life, let him forget it. There will always be attacks.
First from his own family: “Why like this, why like that? Why are you making a fuss, why this, why that? Why [unclear]? Why do you talk like this, why do you talk like that?
Why do you speak the truth? Keep quiet, it's better, keep quiet, you'll fall out with someone,” and so on. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says:

“Do people think that if they say 'we believe' they will be left alone” in peace, to enjoy themselves? You will not, dear brothers, brother, be left to enjoy yourself in peace. When you have said “we believe”, know that you will encounter trial.

Trial – and there is no life in this world without trial. This world is woven through with trials, with thorns. But in Jannah (Paradise), in sha Allah, in sha Allah, there is enjoyment. These are some short messages, but there are many, many of them, we could talk for days, but here are just some short messages so that a person may take a lesson on how to behave in hard times, how to behave in good times, and so on, and so on.

And further, I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who follow the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, truly, as it should be, as befits us believers. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help us and to unite us in Jannah.
Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwa al-Ghafur ar-Rahim.
